policy.description: Blocking line-coverage ratchets. For a fixed scope, coveredLines is the highest value in the reviewed clean-run observation envelope, never a modal or repeated lower value, and that high-water never decreases. Update the envelope in the same reviewed change whenever scope or coverage advances. A fixed-scope floor may move downward only to the exact minimum directly observed by clean runs on the identical source, tests, and total-line scope, with linked evidence and a bounded tolerance; unexplained coverage loss remains a regression.

tolerance.rationale: The issue-666 fix preserves explicit BCP-47 language regions (pt-BR, en-US, es-MX) in media language tags and adds the shared media-language core module with its regional-flag coverage. Rebased onto current main; the official CI client coverage gate measured 2,918/3,304 (88.317%) on this exact tree. coverage-baseline.test.js retains the exact below-floor, above-baseline, scope-change, observed-high-water, and broad-tolerance negative boundaries.

The issue-682 fix preserves direct critic percentages (including zero and single-digit Rotten Tomatoes scores) through every live and full-cache rating-inheritance path and bumps the cache schema to v5 so rows written under the retired CommunityRating-only rule are invalidated. After merging current main (post issue-666), the instrumented scope is 53,179 lines — identical to the pre-merge branch scope, since the merge touched no server lines outside the branch's own changes. Clean runs on this exact source, tests and scope observed 43,479, 43,475, an independent-review 43,484, a hosted-CI high-water of 43,485, and a post-merge local 43,480 covered lines (81.771%). The ten-line envelope is timing-dependent branch coverage in the tag-cache monitor's asynchronous invalidation paths, not a source or test difference; the spread is 0.019 percentage points, far inside the 0.15pp policy bound. coverage-baseline.test.js retains the exact scope-drift, regression, stale-baseline, observed-high-water, spread, single-run, and broad-tolerance negative boundaries.
